text_blocks.snippet: A rotator cuff injury can manifest in several ways, most commonly with pain and limited range of motion in the shoulder. You might experience a dull ache, sharp pain, or even a sensation like your shoulder is catching or clicking when you move. Weakness in the arm, especially when lifting or reaching, is another key sign. To confirm a rotator cuff injury, consult with a doctor who can perform a physical exam and potentially order imaging tests like X-rays, ultrasound, or MRI.
